claims.statement: SystemOneMiddleware plays System 1's top move only when threshold < 1.0 and the gate signal (margin p1-p2 by default, or Choice confidence) is at least the threshold; otherwise it writes a top-k (or top_p prefix capped at k) shortlist as soft candidates, so threshold 0 always plays and threshold 1 never plays.

After a tournament, tournament_threshold replaces threshold when set (otherwise threshold applies), because a final over fewer moves inflates the margin and confidence can depend on the option count; the applied value is recorded as threshold_used.

The System 1 decision is frozen per turn in the private systemone_turn channel and replayed on every later before_model of the same turn instead of re-ranking, writing only current allowed ∩ frozen so later narrowing is never undone and skipped decisions replay as nothing.

In both played and shortlist outcomes SystemOneMiddleware writes System 1's top move as fallback_move (only if still allowed; a skipped decision has none). The UCI adapter uses it as bestmove after a cancellation or execution failure only when the last turn belongs to that search and the move is in the root pool; otherwise it forfeits with the null move 0000 and never plays a random move.

When ranking raises RankingFailed, a middleware with has_model=True records a skipped decision with the error and completed calls and lets the LLM choose unaided, while has_model=False re-raises so the run fails and the turn stays pending.
The tournament seed is turn_seed(agent_seed, turn_id), a SHA-256 of the agent seed and turn id (not hash()), so the shuffle is repeatable within a turn but differs across turns and games.

GatewayRanker ranks with no request when there is one option, with a single systemone.rank request when options fit the model cap (255 for typesafe/jev-* and openai/* models, 16 for any other model), and with a tournament traced as systemone.heats then systemone.final otherwise.

GatewayRanker retries only transient errors (TypeSafe rate limit, connection, timeout and internal server errors, and OpenAI rate limit, connection and internal server errors) up to max_attempts=3 with backoff min(4.0, 0.5*2**n) seconds, fails immediately on other errors, and raises RankingFailed carrying the calls completed before the failure.

Every Choice answer is validated against its own options: unknown labels, non-finite or out-of-range probabilities, an all-zero sum or a sum missing 1 beyond tolerance (widened for two-decimal rounding), bad confidence and a missing Choice answer raise MalformedChoice, which the ranker turns into RankingFailed while keeping the request's Call. Valid answers are only scaled down (divided by max(total, 1)), so a rounded-away shortfall is never inflated, and ties are broken by option order.

The rank request carries a facts-only state (side, FEN, board, material, check, recent SAN) and Choice criteria built from python-chess move facts including static exchange evaluation; the rich style is the default and descriptions are deterministic.

Optional eval Score and needs_calculation/tactics_present Noul questions are added only to the final (or single) request when with_eval/with_nouls are enabled and are recorded as telemetry without affecting the gate.

The tournament shuffles options with random.Random(seed), splits them into ceil(n/cap) balanced heats, advances floor(cap/h) per heat with spare places to the first heats (one each when heats exceed cap, recursing), records single-move heats as byes never sent, packs heats into requests of at most 32 questions, and ends with one final over the finalists.
After a tournament the distribution, shortlist and telemetry top list cover finalists only (flagged finalist_conditional), and each move's stages record per-round results rather than a global rank.

Each classifier request records a Call of kind systemone via make_call, with the model canonicalized as provider:model from the gateway-style name (e.g. typesafe:jev-latest, openai:gpt-6-luna); Jev and OpenAI Decisions report usage and are priced, while a classifier reporting no usage gets cost_usd None.

The shared build_agent in libs/systemone (called by both the server graph and the CLI) wires System 1 by policy: for systemone it builds no model and constructs SystemOneMiddleware with threshold 0, tournament_threshold 0 and has_model False; for hybrid (the default) it passes the settings' gate, threshold, tournament_threshold, k and top_p with has_model True; for llm it builds no ranker and installs NoSystemOne only when fixed_topology is True, otherwise omitting System 1. Surface middleware passed in runs after System 1.

SystemOneMiddleware telemetry is written to Ply.meta["SystemOneMiddleware"] as SystemOneMeta (status, model, top, shortlist, followed, gate, signal, confidence, margin, threshold_used, finalist_conditional, played_move_result, tournament, error, plus NotRequired latency_ms, eval_score, needs_calculation, tactics_present), built from the same payload as systemone_live, and its TypedDicts are mirrored by hand in packages/chess-ui/src/types.ts, where latency_ms, the aux fields and top are optional on SystemOneMeta.

SystemOneMeta.latency_ms is the ranker's wall time for the whole ranking: 0.0 for a local one-option distribution, and for a skipped decision the time the ranking ran before failing (RankingFailed.elapsed_ms). Telemetry is read from the frozen decision, so replays report the first ranking's values.

eval_score, needs_calculation and tactics_present come from an optional Score and two Noul questions that are added only to the aux-bearing (single or final) request when with_eval or with_nouls is enabled. Otherwise, or on skip, they are None, and the gate never uses them.

NoSystemOne has SystemOneMiddleware's name and SystemOneState schema but does nothing in before_model, so the server's fixed-topology graph (policy llm via build_agent with fixed_topology=True, and the credential-free shape() graph) keeps the same nodes and state keys as a graph running System 1.

On the server, System 1 classifiers share per-process HTTP client pools from clients.py (15 s timeout, created lazily under a lock): POOL holds an httpx2 sync/async pair for TypeSafe and DECISIONS_POOL an httpx pair for OpenAI Decisions. The FastAPI app lifespan closes both on shutdown, after which get() creates a fresh pair. The pools live in their own module because langgraph loads graph.py under a generated module name.

SystemOneMiddleware reports the frozen decision's ranking time through turn_latency_ms, so the ranking is counted once per turn across retries: a System 1 move's ply and turn latency equal the ranking time, and a hybrid turn adds it to model time.

With no injected client, GatewayRanker builds its classifier lazily on first use so graph construction needs no credentials: OpenAIDecisions wrapped in DecisionsClassifier (max_retries=0) for openai/<model>, otherwise TypeSafeClassifier(model, timeout=15 s). Its async path builds the request (including move descriptions) in a worker thread via asyncio.to_thread.

The ranker comes from a ranker_factory: the CLI uses default_ranker, a plain GatewayRanker built from the settings' systemone_model, style, with_eval and with_nouls with a lazily created client, while the server's pooled_ranker injects a client chosen by model name: a Decisions classifier using LANGSMITH_GATEWAY* credentials for openai/<model>, otherwise a TypeSafeClassifier using TYPESAFE_API_KEY/TYPESAFE_BASE_URL from ServerSettings.typesafe(), which raises ValueError when either is missing; because it runs only inside the ranker factory, only policies that run a TypeSafe System 1 need these credentials.

System 1's knobs (systemone_model typesafe/jev-latest, style rich, with_eval and with_nouls False, gate margin, threshold 0.9, tournament_threshold null, k 5 up to 255, top_p null, seed 0) and policy (default hybrid) are fields of ChessContext in libs/systemone settings.py, which is also the versioned JSON settings file format (version 3) with forward migrations and rejection of newer versions; the migration to version 3 replaces any retired semif-* System 1 model with Jev.

The CLI's opponent settings come from an optional --config settings file loaded with load_file, then overridden by each given flag, with --reset putting named settings back to their defaults; the server resolves settings from the assistant context first and then config configurable keys, treating a missing version as current, dropping unknown keys, letting an explicit null reset a setting to its default, and validating the merged values up front.
The tournament's agent seed is the opponent's seed setting (ChessContext.seed), which build_agent passes to create_chess_agent.

On first ranking SystemOneMiddleware also writes the decision to the public systemone_live channel (output but never input), so clients can show System 1's result before the LLM answers; it carries turn_id and the turn's System 1 calls, is never cleared, and is not rewritten when a retry replays the frozen decision.

DecisionsClassifier adapts OpenAIDecisions to the ranker's TypeSafe-shaped Classifier, translating Choice, Score and Noul questions and answers both ways; a refusal is dropped, so the ranker reads the missing answer as malformed and the ranking fails.

Because a chess position has at most 218 legal moves, below the 255-option cap of Jev and OpenAI Decisions, tournaments only run for classifiers on the default 16-option cap (or an explicit smaller max_options).
